column1: # DARWIN LINK-NAME ORACLE — what a REAL platform compiler emits for each C
# identifier the shipped descriptors import on Mach-O, per arch.
# every Mach-O-visible imported function in `src/dss-config/shippedLibs/**` to
# have a row here AND to declare the `linkName` this row implies. A symbol added
# to a descriptor without a row here goes RED — which is the whole point: the
# fixed table in `test_shipped_lib_descriptor.cpp` pins the eight names that
# diverge TODAY, and this file pins that no NEW symbol has started to.
# WHY AN ORACLE AND NOT AN EXPORT CHECK. "verify the symbol is exported" does NOT
# catch this class: BOTH `_fstat` and `_fstat$INODE64` exist in libSystem's
# x86_64 slice, so an export check answers YES for the WRONG one. Declaring the
# plain name there binds the LEGACY 32-bit-inode callee while DSS compiles the
# modern 144-byte `struct stat` — 120 bytes written into 144, `st_size` read at
# 96 and written at 72, `fstat` returns 0, and sqlite calls every database
# "database disk image is malformed". It links clean and loads clean. The only
# question that separates the two spellings is the one this file answers.
#   `symbol`      the C identifier a descriptor declares (keyed by NAME, not by
#                 descriptor: 41 identifiers are declared by two descriptors —
#                 math/tgmath, string/memory, unistd/sys.sysctl — and the link
#                 name is a property of the PLATFORM, so the two must agree).
#   `probeHeader` the header the measurement included. USUALLY the descriptor's
#                 own `header`, but 16 rows differ because DSS's shipped headers
#                 are a deliberate SUPERSET of the platform's: `statfs`/`fstatfs`
#                 live in DSS's <unistd.h> and in Darwin's <sys/mount.h>,
#                 `setlocale` in DSS's <stdlib.h> and Darwin's <locale.h>, and so
#                 on. Recorded per row because a probe that guesses the header
#                 reports `<compile-failed>` and would silently measure NOTHING
#                 for exactly the symbols most likely to be renamed — `statfs`
#                 and `fstatfs` are TWO OF THE EIGHT that diverge.
#   `emitted-*`   the EXACT undefined symbol `nm -u` printed, DECORATED (Mach-O's
#                 leading `_` included) because that is what the tool printed and
#                 a table of measurements must not silently edit its readings.
#                 The test strips the format's decoration itself, through the
# HOW TO REGENERATE (needs a real Mac; `scripts/ssh-macos/ssh-macos.sh` reaches
# the operator's). Per symbol, per arch:
# Exactly one undefined symbol comes back; that is the cell. A `<compile-failed>`
# means the probe header is wrong for THIS platform — fix `probeHeader`, never
# MEASURED 2026-08-25 on macOS 26.5.2 (Darwin 25.5.0, arm64 host), Apple `cc`
# probes, every one returning exactly one undefined symbol. EIGHT diverge:
# stat fstat lstat statfs fstatfs opendir readdir (x86_64 only, `$INODE64`) and
# realpath (BOTH arches, `$DARWIN_EXTSN`). No other identifier is renamed on
